searchDocs.content: DrawVents The duct tools: a vent that runs along X or Z and turns at right angles, a sloped vent and a vertical shaft. searchDocs.content: OpeningTools The tools that cut an opening into a plain wall: doorway, window, circle window, triangle window and archway. The opening is centered on the cursor. searchDocs.title: Bend​
searchDocs.content: </> Paths.Bend( joint: Vector3 ,-- where the two segments meet, at the base level prevDir: Vector3 ,-- the direction of the earlier segment dir: Vector3 ,-- the direction of the new segment prevStrips: {Strip},-- the strips of the earlier segment strips: {Strip}-- the strips of the new segment ) → Bend-- finish and start are keyed by strip key, in studs along each segment's direction Closes the corner where a wall or corridor continues another, with an exact miter and no overlap. Each strip (a wall, a floor) is cut along the line that bisects the bend: the strip keeps a plain rectangle up to the shorter end of that cut, and a small triangular prism fills the rest. A right angle needs no triangle: the earlier strip runs on to cover the corner square. The earlier segment's rectangles move by finish and the new segment's by start; the triangles go in ending and beginning.

searchDocs.title: The layers​
searchDocs.content: Each layer only requires the layers below it.  Plugin.server.luau entry: toolbar buttons, dock widget, starts the app App/ composition root, user actions, raw input Ui/ the panel (vide): Panel shell, Controls, one file per tab in Pages/ Tools/ Modal/ the active tool, and the modal actions (extrude, grab/rotate/scale) Services/ State/ shared state and services the tools and panel use Core/ Roblox-facing libraries: geometry, builders, cutting, overlay, colors Pure/ plain data and maths, no Roblox API, tested under Lune   Folder	What lives thereApp/App.luau	Creates every service and wires them together. The one place that does. Read it first. App/Actions.luau	Every user intent (Esc, Enter, X/Y/Z, H, tab changes, scroll stepping…). Hotkeys and panel buttons both call these. App/Input.luau	Raw input → actions: key presses through Pure/Keymap, typed digits, clicks, the wheel. State/Store.luau	The settings. Tools read store.Values freely; all writes go through Store.Set/Mutate. State/AppState.luau	vide sources for what the panel shows: active mode, working folder, status line, tab… Services/	Cursor (mouse ray, snapping), Edit (undo recording), Status (messages), Display (pastel, grid, hidden parts), WorkingFolder, CameraLight, Admin (who works in the folder, and its admin). Tools/	One module per tool family behind the contract in Tools/Types.luau; Runner runs the active one; Registry lists them. Tools/Draw/	The 19 point-to-point tools: Engine (the shared drawing flow) and one small file per family of shapes. Modal/	Extrude (T) and Move (G, R, C, D) behind Modal/Types.luau; Host runs the active one and the armed flip/rotate. Ui/	Panel (shell), Controls (number field, switch, slider, choice row…), Popups (tooltip, reset menu), Pages/. Core/	Builders/ (what each shape is made of, one file per family: Paths, Areas, Railings, Slopes, Openings, Vents, Place, with shared Shapes), Geometry (specs → parts, unions), Joints (cutting holes), Overlay (viewport drawing), Colors, SurfaceGrid, Snapper, VentHoles (remembered vent holes), Transform, Arrange, Hidden, Brushes, Sounds, Props. Pure/	Settings, Keymap, Tools (labels, glyphs, instructions, tiles), PropData, AxisLock, NumericInput, Polygon, Snap, Cycle, Tips, SoundIds, AdminRules.

searchDocs.title: How a frame flows​
searchDocs.content: Heartbeat ─► Modal/Host.Step (an active extrude or grab follows the mouse) ─► WorkingFolder.Step (folder outlines, deleted-folder check) ─► every 0.05 s: Runner.Step ─► tool.Preview(ctx, state) ─► Overlay draws ghosts, cut, snap mark, holes Mouse click ─► Input ─► WorkingFolder.Click (while picking) ─► Host.Confirm (while a modal action runs) ─► Runner.Click ─► fresh Preview ─► tool.Click ─► ctx.Edit(...) builds Key press ─► Input ─► typed digit? into Host/Runner numeric entry ─► Keymap.Resolve ─► Actions.Perform   Every change to the place goes through ctx.Edit(name, fn) (Services/Edit), which makes it one undo step, cancels it cleanly on error and hands new parts to pastel colors and the surface grid.

searchDocs.title: The tool contract​
searchDocs.content: A tool (see Tools/Types.luau) is a table of functions plus a state table it makes in Begin. All of a tool's state lives in that table, so leaving or resetting a tool drops it, and nothing one tool does can leak into the next. The runner is the only caller.  Function	When	RuleBegin(ctx)	the tool is picked	return the fresh state Preview(ctx, state)	~20 times a second	read the mouse, return what to draw; never change the place Click(ctx, state, preview)	left click	change the place only through ctx.Edit Back(ctx, state)	Esc	undo one step and return a message, or nil to leave the tool Confirm, Lock, Typing, Release, Refresh, Busy, Finish	optional	see the type's doc comment

searchDocs.title: Adding a tool​
searchDocs.content: Write Tools/MyTool.luau returning { tool } (or add a shape to a Tools/Draw/ file; a draw shape only needs Id, Start and Build).Add it to FAMILIES in Tools/Registry.luau.Add its label, glyph and description to Tools.List and its instruction toTools.Instructions in Pure/Tools.luau, and put its id in a tile of Tools.Grid. The Lune tests fail if one of these is missing.Add its option rows to Ui/Pages/Build.luau, each with the modes it belongs to.

searchDocs.title: Adding a setting​
searchDocs.content: Add the field and its default to Pure/Settings.luau (Settings type and Defaults).Show it with Controls.Number/Switch/Choice using its Key; the control reads and writes the Store, saves, and offers a right-click reset to the default.If changing it must restyle something already in the map, add a Store.Watch inServices/Display.luau. Never special-case it in the panel.

searchDocs.title: Where to look when something breaks​
searchDocs.content: Symptom	Start inA tool's preview or build is wrong	its file under Tools/ (find it in Tools/Registry); for a draw tool, its shape in Tools/Draw/, then Engine What a shape is made of (sizes, pieces)	its family in Core/Builders/ A cut or hole is wrong, or rooms do not join	Core/Joints.luau A point snaps to the wrong place	Tools/Draw/Points.luau, Services/Cursor.luau, Core/Snapper.luau A key does the wrong thing	Pure/Keymap.luau (which action), App/Input.luau (when it is ignored), App/Actions.luau (what it does) Esc / Enter misbehave	Actions.Cancel / Actions.Confirm, then the tool's Back / Confirm A panel row shows at the wrong time	its Visible in Ui/Pages/*.luau A panel value is stale	it is not reading Store.Get / an AppState source reactively, or something wrote around the Store Pastel colors, surface grid, hidden parts	Services/Display.luau, then Core/Colors, Core/SurfaceGrid, Core/Hidden Working folder, tags, shared settings	Services/WorkingFolder.luau Who is admin, a control greyed for someone	Services/Admin.luau, then Pure/AdminRules.luau Undo is wrong or an edit is half-applied	Services/Edit.luau and the ctx.Edit call in the tool Something leaks after reloading the plugin	a connection not given to a trove or vide.cleanup

searchDocs.title: Rules that keep it this way​
searchDocs.content: Settings are written only through the Store. Assigning into store.Values directly leaves the panel stale and skips saving.Services are created only in App/App.luau. Pass what a module needs in its Deps.A tool keeps its state in its state table, never in module-level locals.The panel holds no logic. It shows AppState and the Store and calls App/Actions or a service. Anything worth testing goes in Pure/.Connections are cleaned up: into a Trove (services, tools such as Extend keep their own) orvide.cleanup (panel).vide runs with strict and defaults off (set in App.new). Strict mode would run effects twice, doubling side effects; vide's instance defaults differ from Roblox's.

searchDocs.title: Checks​
searchDocs.content: npm run verify runs StyLua, Selene, the Lune tests, both Rojo builds, and a strict luau-lsptype check of src (Roblox type definitions are cached in .luau-analyze/). Green means the code is well-formed and type-correct. It does not mean the tools work: that is checked by hand in Studio.

searchDocs.title: 1. Make a working folder​
searchDocs.content: The plugin only builds and edits inside one working folder. Nothing outside it is touched.  Make a Folder in Workspace, for example Map.Tag it: select the folder, open View > Tag Editor and add the tag VluxyBT_Map.  The tag is a safety catch, so the plugin can't change a folder by mistake, and it is required. Pick a folder without it and the panel shows a red notice saying how to tag it; once tagged, it is picked.

searchDocs.title: 2. Pick the folder​
searchDocs.content: In the Working Folder card at the top of the panel, click Choose working folder.Click any part inside the folder in the viewport, or select the folder in the Explorer. The folder gets an outline and the panel asks Work in this folder?Click Yes. Click Cancel (or press Esc) to back out.  If the folder already holds shared settings from a teammate that differ from yours, the panel names them and offers three buttons:  Button	What happensUse folder's	You take the settings saved on the folder. Overwrite	Your settings are saved onto the folder. Cancel	You keep your current working folder.  See Teams for which settings are shared. Next time you open the place, the plugin offers the folder you last worked in.

searchDocs.title: 3. Draw a wall​
searchDocs.content: Press Ctrl+1 (or click the Basic tile) and pick Walls.Click a start point on the ground, then click an end point. The wall is built.Keep clicking to add more walls to the chain. Press Enter to start a new chain.  While drawing:  Hold Shift to snap to the fine grid.Press X or Z to lock to an axis. Press it again to unlock.Type a number, such as 16, for an exact length.Press Y to drag the height with the mouse, or use [ and ].

searchDocs.title: 4. Draw a room​
searchDocs.content: Press Ctrl+4 (Structures) and pick Room.Click two opposite corners. You get a floor and four walls.  Rooms drawn against each other join up. The Open, Shared and Separate buttons choose whether the rooms share no wall, one wall, or keep both.

searchDocs.title: 5. Add a door​
searchDocs.content: Press Ctrl+3 (Additive) and pick Doorway.Click a plain wall. The doorway is centred on the cursor.Move the mouse to set how deep the cut goes, then click. Past the far side, it cuts all the way through. (Turn off Set cut depth with mouse to cut through in one click.)  By default you get a doorway with a frame and a see-through door panel.

searchDocs.title: 6. Undo and stop​
searchDocs.content: Ctrl+Z undoes a build. Every build is one undo step.Esc or a right-click drops the point you are drawing from. Press it again to stop the tool.Pressing a tool's Ctrl+number again also stops it. Enter with no tool on brings back the last one.  The status line in the panel always says what to do next. Next: Tools.

searchDocs.title: Themes​
searchDocs.content: Turn on Themes (or press P) to color the parts in your working folder. Pick a theme from the six buttons, or hold P and scroll to switch.  Theme	What it colors byPastel	A random soft color for every part. Unity	What the part is: walls grey; floors, ceilings and stairs orange. Levels	Building level: one color per floor of the building, from the ground up. Structures	One bold color per room, corridor or model. Facing	Direction, so crooked parts stand out. Size	Size, from yellow (small) to violet (big).  In every theme, a part that is partly see-through is purple.  The Facing colors:  Color	PartBlue	Runs along X Green	Runs along Z Orange	Diagonal Tan	Flat Grey	Square, with no clear direction Magenta	Tilted off level  The Size colors go yellow (under 1 stud), green (under 4), teal (under 12), blue (under 32), then violet for anything bigger.  New parts the plugin builds take the theme color straight away, in the same undo step.

searchDocs.title: Surface grid​
searchDocs.content: Turn on Surface grid (or press L) to put a grid texture on every part in the working folder.  Grid tile size sets how many studs one tile covers.Pick a grid color from the swatches, or type a hex code such as FF8A24.  The grid stays on, even after you close and reopen Studio, until you switch it off.

searchDocs.title: Camera light​
searchDocs.content: Camera light (or Alt+L) adds a light that follows your camera, for building in dark places. Set its Light range and Light brightness. The light is never saved into the place, and only you see it.

searchDocs.title: Hidden parts​
searchDocs.content: Select parts and press H to hide them. Hiding is shared: the parts disappear for everyone in Team Create, and only the folder's admin can hide or unhide. A hidden part is locked, so clicks and the tools pass through it. Hiding and Unhide all are each one undo step.  Control	What it doesShow hidden parts (ghosted) (or I)	Show hidden parts as faint ghosts instead of not at all. Only on your screen. Ghost transparency	How see-through the ghosts are. searchDocs.title: The admin​
searchDocs.content: Studio sends every change to a part to the whole team, so the things everyone sees can only be decided by one person. Each working folder has one admin.  The admin is whoever has had the plugin open on the folder the longest. Someone working alone is always the admin.When the admin closes the plugin, changes folder or stops answering for about 45 seconds, admin passes to the next person who has been there longest.The Working Folder card's title line shows a face for everyone in the folder. The admin's has a ring; hover a face to see the name.The admin can click someone's face and pick Give admin. Anyone else can click a face and pickRequest admin; the admin then sees the request on the card and picks Give or Ignore. A request runs out after a minute.Someone who has done nothing in Studio for more than 15 minutes is idle: their face is faded and hovering it adds "idle 17 min". Idle never moves admin by itself, but when the admin is idle, anyone else in the folder can click the admin's face and pick Take over admin to become admin at once.

searchDocs.title: How idle is detected​
searchDocs.content: Your plugin counts any of these as activity: a key or mouse button press, moving the mouse or turning the mouse wheel, moving the camera, typing in a script, changing the selection, undo, redo, and any finished edit. It writes the time of your last activity onto the folder asVluxyBT_Active_<userId>, at most once a minute and only after new activity, so idle times are about a minute coarse. The times come from each person's computer clock, so a clock that is far off makes someone look more or less idle than they are. Someone using an older plugin that writes no activity counts from when they joined.  Only the admin can change these. For everyone else the controls are greyed, hovering them names the admin, and their hotkeys and toolbar buttons only say so in the status line:  What	WhereThemes on or off, and which theme	Display tab, the toolbar, P, hold P and scroll Surface grid on or off, tile size and color	Display tab, the toolbar, L Ghost transparency	Display tab Hiding parts and Unhide all	H, Alt+H, Display tab Whose settings a folder keeps (Use folder's or Overwrite)	Working Folder card  Everyone keeps every build tool, Arrange, Props, the camera light, the ghost view (I), their own Settings tab and hint bar.  Who is in a folder is kept in attributes on the folder: VluxyBT_Here_<userId> (the last heartbeat, every 15 seconds), VluxyBT_Joined_<userId>, VluxyBT_Active_<userId>, VluxyBT_Admin andVluxyBT_AdminRequest. They are cleared when you leave and are not undo steps.

searchDocs.title: Shared through the folder​
searchDocs.content: These settings are saved as attributes on the working folder, so everyone working in it shares them:  Setting	Where the admin sets itThe theme	Display tab, or hold P and scroll Ghost transparency	Display tab, Hidden parts card Themes on or off	Display tab, P, or the toolbar Surface grid on or off	Display tab, L, or the toolbar Grid tile size and grid color	Display tab  When the admin changes one, it is written to the folder and everyone takes it over.  When you pick a folder whose shared settings differ from yours and nobody else is working in it, you choose Use folder's (take theirs), Overwrite (save yours onto the folder) orCancel. If teammates are already working in it, you simply take the folder's settings.  The theme colors and the surface grid are real changes to the parts, so everyone sees them. The shared on/off switches decide whether they come back on by themselves when someone opens the plugin. If you close the plugin while a teammate still has it open, the colors and grid stay on for them.

searchDocs.title: Hidden parts are shared​
searchDocs.content: When the admin hides a part (H), it gets the VluxyBT_Hidden tag and is locked. Tags and locks reach the whole team, and every copy of the plugin hides tagged parts on its own screen, so the part disappears for everyone. The tools aim through hidden parts. Undo brings a hidden part back.

searchDocs.title: Unit specs​
searchDocs.content: npm test runs lune run tests/runner, which loads every *.spec.luau under tests/. Pass a word to run only the specs whose path holds it, such as lune run tests/runner Openings.  A spec returns a table of cases. Each case gets expect, whose checks (equal, near, truthy,falsy, errors) throw on failure:  return { ["a foundation is wider by the margin"] = function(expect) expect.equal(#specs, 1) end, }   tests/Pure/ requires src/Pure modules directly. They touch no Roblox API.tests/Core/ loads the builders, Geometry, Snapper and Transform throughtests/Support/Harness.luau. The harness gives each module its own require, real Roblox datatypes and Parts from Lune's @lune/roblox, and a real DataModel as game, so a spec runs the plugin's own code.  The harness cannot fake everything. Raycasts, GetPartBoundsInRadius, instance signals, CSG, ChangeHistoryService and plugin APIs are left untested here. Two Lune gaps are worked around:Harness.SyncPositions fills in BasePart.Position, which Lune does not derive from CFrame, and Harness.CFrame corrects CFrame.lookAt, which Lune 0.10.5 gets wrong for any direction with a Z part.

searchDocs.title: Benchmarks​
searchDocs.content: npm run perf runs lune run tests/perf. Each *.bench.luau in tests/Perf/ returns named benchmarks with a Budget in milliseconds and a Run function. The runner times each one, prints a table of the median time against its budget, and exits with an error if any is over.  Budgets are about three times a measured run, so they fail only on a real slowdown. Timings depend on the machine, which is why npm run verify leaves them out. Raise a budget only when the extra work is intended.

searchDocs.title: Studio smoke script​
searchDocs.content: Some behaviour needs a real place: raycasts, spatial queries and the color sweep.tests/Studio/Smoke.luau is a command-bar script that builds into a temporary folder, prints one [VluxyTest] PASS or FAIL line per check, and cleans up. See tests/Studio/README.md for how to run it.
